san_disambiguation_bug_below.what: gigachess' move generator reads the cached `checkers` bitboard, and `Board::play_fast` (v0.1.4) leaves that cache stale. SAN disambiguation therefore resolved its candidates against a stale king-safety answer while the exporter walked with `play_fast`.
san_disambiguation_bug_below.symptom: five games of 11,149,374 rendered under-disambiguated SAN: Rg6 for Rfg6 (game 430595), Rxb1 for Raxb1 (2312993), Qxb7 for Q8xb7 (2591629), Re7 for R8e7 (2722771), Qxg4 for Qcxg4 (3048647) - eight bytes of output in total.
san_disambiguation_bug_below.fix: `MoveSink::wants_checkers` (default false) makes the writer's tree answer true, so the walk makes moves with `Board::play` and the cache is current; the cost is +2 ns per make, and the saving is one board copy, one make_move_unchecked and one unmake_move per ply.
san_disambiguation_bug_below.evidence: a two-mode renderer over the whole database (each game's movetext rendered with the maintained and with the stale cache) reports exactly those five games, and a whole-database invariant run asserts body+suffix equals move_to_san for all 11,149,374 games' every ply
san_disambiguation_bug_below.gold_parity: unchanged: 407,350 matched / 50 annotation / 3 other / 5 tags, 0 read errors - the five games lie outside the 419,385-game gold range
san_disambiguation_bug_below.lesson: a fast move that skips a cache a later call trusts is not merely faster, it is wrong; the contract is now on the sink trait and pinned by tests/san_split.rs

second_round_inline_san_and_write_path.change: pgn-export-sota-performance, after the archive: the SAN inline in its node, no per-game String or Vec, one game per buffer and one write_all, tag heads as literals, tiny memcpys as byte pushes, pooled parallel chunk buffers
what: the SAN body and its check/mate suffix live in the node (gigachess hands the body over in a fixed-size San by value), so the walk records a move with no copy and the shared text buffer is gone

no per-game String for the ECO tag (the three ASCII bytes of the code), no per-game Vec for the traversal's step stack (the writer's buffer), one buffer per game for tags + movetext + result + blank line, and one write_all per game
one literal per tag head, and the one-to-three byte writes (the move number's '. ', the tag's closing quote, the separators) as byte pushes instead of push_str's memcpy call
NameBuf::set takes ASCII names without a UTF-8 validation pass
the parallel pipeline recycles its chunk buffers, each sized from the run's high-water mark (a megabase chunk is ~5.6 MiB, so a fresh buffer grew into it by doubling)

second_round_inline_san_and_write_path.not_done_and_why: the full single-copy movetext stays infeasible (see the archived task 7.1): a side line is stored before the main continuation it belongs to, and MoveSink::branch fires after any move followed by a line change, so the walk cannot own the layout or the forced numbers. What it would still save is the per-move SAN copy, which needs unsafe to beat the memcpy call - the workspace warns on unsafe and the gain does not justify it.

buffer_sweep.question: is the 1 MiB write buffer and the 8,192-record chunk the right pair, or does a bigger buffer go faster?
buffer_sweep.method: the two knobs are now flags on the `megabase` example (`--pgn-buffer BYTES`, `--pgn-batch RECORDS`); each row is a whole run with `/usr/bin/time -l`, on the reference database, to /dev/null and to a file on the internal SSD

write_buffer_single_thread_to_a_file.reading: 64 KiB to 16 MiB is 1.5 % of the wall clock for 17 MB of resident memory; 1 MiB is on the plateau and 16 MiB is inside the same run-to-run range

write_buffer_ten_threads_to_dev_null_thr.reading: medians 5.24 / 5.19 / 5.17 / 5.10 s: 2.7 % from 256 KiB to 16 MiB, which is the size of the spread inside each configuration; the sink buffer is one allocation for the whole process, so 15 MB more of it is 0.2 % of the 7.3 GB peak

chunk_size_ten_threads.reading: the knee is 8,192-16,384: 16,384 buys 2.1 % for +60 MB, 65,536 buys 4.7 % for +390 MB. 8,192 stays the default, on the knee, and the flag is there for a caller who wants the last 2 %
chunk_size_ten_threads.single_thread: 34.16-34.37 s across 1,024 to 32,768 records per chunk: the chunk size does not matter with one worker, only the pipeline's memory and its load balance do

buffer_sweep.conclusion: the defaults are at the knee, not on a slope: raising the write buffer buys at most a couple of per cent for 0.2 % more memory and no measurable gain, and raising the chunk size trades memory for a few per cent. Both are tunable per run now, and neither default changes.
buffer_sweep.side_fix: `--pgn-last` only reached the parallel path before this round; the sequential walk ignored it and exported the whole database. It bounds both now, which is what the sweeps above needed.
